Team + Ops,

I want to propose a coordinated maintenance window and canary ramp for the upcoming private deployment patch (v2.8.1 -> v2.9.0). This is for FinBank Corp (VPC private deployment). Goal: apply security/OS + runtime patches while preserving pinned model versions and ensuring fast rollback if regressions appear.

High-level proposal (attached runbook + canary matrix):
- Maintenance window: target weekdays only, 02:00–06:00 PT; prefer Sun->Mon overnight for least traffic.
- Staged canary: 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% over 2-hour increments (canary_matrix_20270515.csv attached).
- Version pinning: serve layer will keep model pin v2.8.x; runtime will run compatibility shim for v2.9.0. No automatic model upgrades during window.
- Rollback triggers: latency > 2.5x baseline OR error-rate bump > 1.5pp OR functional regression on smoke prompts. Immediate rollback to v2.8.1 with KV cache preservation.
- Preflight: smoke set (20 prompts), KV cache snapshot, backup of local config, control-plane snapshot.
- Networking: ensure firewall ports xxxxx remain open, CIDR exceptions for our canary hosts, and route-reflectors warmed before cutover.
- Communication: Ops to provide out-of-band PagerDuty contact; we’ll open status doc and update every 15 minutes.

Action items for this thread: please review and respond by EOD Monday with:
1) Ops preferred maintenance date(s) and any blackout windows.
2) Ben: confirm if KV cache snapshot approach is safe for the runtime path.
3) Marissa: legal/compliance notes for FinBank (retention/audit log needs).

Attaching: redwood_private_maintenance_runbook_v1.3.pdf (runbook draft), canary_matrix_20270515.csv

Thanks,
Dev

Quick technical callouts:

- KV cache snapshot: we should snapshot active KV ranges and the LRU mapping. Restoring the mapping is required to avoid cache poisoning and serving mismatch; snapshot should be stored to S3-compatible storage with TTL 7 days.
- Model pin header verification: add an automated assert in the post-deploy smoke that queries /metadata for pin_version and fails the job if mismatch.
- Canary sizing: 2% -> 10% -> 25% looks reasonable, but add a gating step at 10% where we run a small set (50) of latency-sensitive calls through the canary path for 15 minutes.
- Config drift: ensure that the configmap merge during deploy is an overlay (not replace) — we had an incident in Q1 where replace removed a TLS option.

I'll add these items into the runbook and send an updated PDF by EOD.
